# DS-01: Python and Data Wrangling (Tier 1)

**Subtrack:** Data Science  
**Unit scope:** Idiomatic Python, NumPy and pandas/Polars for reshaping, joining, aggregating and vectorising tabular data.

**Tier note:** Tier 3 is not offered. Advanced wrangling is assessed inside DS-11 (pipelines) and DS-12 (research), where it serves a purpose instead of being an end in itself.

## Assessments

Pick **any one**. Every assessment here is an independent, complete demonstration of this unit at this tier.

- **[DS-T1-001](DS-T1-001-the-price-watch-bulletin/README.md): The Price Watch Bulletin: From Spreadsheet Export to Tidy Data.** Reshape a print-formatted, multi-table state food price bulletin (merged headers, page breaks, footnote notation, summary rows) into tested tidy data, then recompute every published average to discover how the national figure is really built and which averages are inconsistent.
- **[DS-T1-002](DS-T1-002-the-ledger-that-double-counts/README.md): The Ledger That Double-Counts: Debugging a Mobile-Money Settlement Pipeline.** A legacy POS agent-banking settlement script runs cleanly but pays the wrong commission. Find every defect against its docstring specification, prove each with a failing test, fix it, reconcile with the switch's control totals, and measure what each defect cost.
- **[DS-T1-003](DS-T1-003-rain-onset-at-scale/README.md): Rain Onset at Scale: Vectorising an Agro-Climate Pipeline Without Changing Its Answers.** Profile a correct but loop-bound rainfall pipeline (monthly totals, dry spells, agronomic onset dates, anomalies), re-implement it with NumPy and pandas, prove equivalence against the legacy oracle on adversarial inputs, and measure the speed-up with a fair benchmark protocol.
